items.title: Merit and Wisdom's Own Cause and Fruit — Sorting the Six Perfections into Three Clean Categories

items.zh: 云何為福？云何為智？謂略說福，即是三種波羅蜜多。一、施波羅蜜多，二、戒波羅蜜多，三、忍波羅蜜多。智唯一種波羅蜜多。謂慧波羅蜜多。精進、靜慮波羅蜜多，應知通二分。一者、福分，二者、智分。
items.en: What is merit? What is wisdom? In brief, merit is three perfections: giving, precepts, and patience. Wisdom is only one perfection: the perfection of wisdom itself. Diligence and concentration, one should know, belong to both divisions — partly to merit, and partly to wisdom.

items.zh: 若依精進修行布施、受護淨戒，及修慈等四種無量，如是等類所有精進，名為福分。若依精進習聞思修所成三慧，修蘊善巧、修界善巧、修處善巧、修緣起善巧、修處非處善巧，修能觀察苦為真苦、集為真集、滅為真滅、道為真道，及於一切善不善法，有罪、無罪、若劣、若勝、若黑、若白，并廣分別緣生法中，皆能如實思擇觀察，如是等類所有精進，名為智分。
items.en: Diligence exercised in practising giving, upholding and guarding pure precepts, and cultivating loving-kindness and the other three immeasurables — this kind of diligence is called the portion belonging to merit. Diligence exercised in cultivating the wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and meditation, in skillfulness regarding the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, and valid reasoning, and in observing suffering as truly suffering, origin as truly origin, cessation as truly cessation, and the path as truly the path — this kind of diligence is called the portion belonging to wisdom.

items.zh: 若依靜慮，修習慈等四種無量，如是等類所有靜慮，名為福分。若依靜慮，能修如前精進中說蘊善巧等，如是等類所有靜慮，名為智分。如是福智略有六種；一一分別，應知無量。云何福因？云何智因？

items.title: Section: Merit and Wisdom Complete — Merit Is Most Excellent, Wisdom Is Unsurpassed, Neither Alone Suffices

items.zh: 略說應知福因、智因總有三種。一者、於福於智，能得、能住、能增長欲；二者、於福於智，善能隨順無違背緣；三者、於福於智，先已串習。
items.en: In brief, one should know there are, in total, three causes for both merit and wisdom: first, the wish to attain, sustain, and increase them; second, favourable conditions genuinely free of obstruction; third, prior habituation with them.

items.zh: 此中隨順無違背緣者，謂顛倒緣不現在前不會遇性，不顛倒緣正現在前正會遇性。若遇惡友倒說福智，或倒作意顛倒而取，名顛倒緣現前會遇；與此相違所有白品，當知名為不顛倒緣現前會遇。若於福智能得、能住及能增長，勤修習障遠離不起，當知是名無違背緣。若諸菩薩於此三種福智因中隨有所闕，當知不能生福、生智。云何福果？云何智果？
謂諸菩薩依止福故，雖復長時流轉生死，不為極苦之所損惱；又隨所欲能攝眾生，為作義利。依止智故，所攝受福是正非邪；又能起作種種無量善巧事業，乃至究竟當證無上正等菩提。
items.en: Resting on merit, bodhisattvas, though cycling through birth and death for a long time, are never afflicted by the most extreme suffering, and are able, as they wish, to gather beings and accomplish genuine benefit for them … resting on wisdom, the merit thereby gathered is correct rather than deviant, and one is able to undertake boundless skilful works, ultimately realising unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.zh: 如是略說福果、智果，如其所應當知四種；品類差別，復有無量。
應知此中若異熟體、若異熟因、若異熟果，如是一切皆依於福，從福所生；福復依智，從智所起。是故二種，於證無上正等菩提雖俱是勝；而於其中福為最勝，智為無上。若諸菩薩於福、於智隨闕一種，決定不能證於無上正等菩提。
items.en: One should know that the ripened body, its cause, and its fruit — all of this rests upon merit, arising from merit; and merit in turn rests upon wisdom, arising from wisdom … therefore, though both are excellent for realising unsurpassed, perfect awakening, merit is the more excellent of the two, and wisdom the more unsurpassed. Should a bodhisattva lack either merit or wisdom, awakening can never, under any circumstance, be realised.

items.zh: 是名菩薩因攝果攝自利利他。云何菩薩現法後法自利利他？

items.title: Section: This-Life and Next-Life Benefit — Four Things a Bodhisattva Rightly Enjoys in the Present

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩以如正理工巧業處士夫作用積集財物，即於如是所集財物知量受用。
items.en: Bodhisattvas accumulate wealth through lawful skill and honest human effort, and, having accumulated it, make use of it with a sense of proportion … once accumulated, they are not defiled by it, do not dwell on it, do not crave it, are not bound by it, do not grieve over it, are not attached to it, and do not clutch it tightly — seeing deeply into its dangers, and using it with a clear understanding oriented towards renunciation. This is called using it with a sense of proportion.

items.zh: 又先所造可愛果業異熟果熟，於現法中受用彼果。又諸菩薩於諸靜慮善迴轉者，為欲獲得現法樂住，於現法中依此靜慮；不為成立利他事故，依此靜慮。又諸如來現法涅槃，所有世間及出世間一切能得現法涅槃諸有為法。
items.en: Also, when the karmic fruit of previously created desirable actions ripens, one enjoys that fruit in this very life … also, bodhisattvas already skilled in freely entering and leaving the dhyānas may, wishing simply to obtain the bliss of dwelling in the present dhyāna itself, rest in that dhyāna for its own sake, not in order to accomplish some benefit for others … also, the Tathāgatas' own nirvāṇa realised in this very life rests on every mundane and supramundane conditioned factor capable of bringing about that present-life nirvāṇa.

items.zh: 是名菩薩現法自利。如諸菩薩現法自利，如是菩薩所化有情，由此獲得現法利益，當知即是現法利他。若於欲界能獲他世財寶具足、自體具足，及能當生靜慮、無色；若生靜慮及無色中，能獲他世財寶具足、自體具足；若現法中與憂苦俱，數數思擇修習善因，是名菩薩修習後法自利利他。若諸菩薩於現法中與喜樂俱，修習當來財寶具足、自體具足所有善因，及非退分靜慮、無色一切等至，是名菩薩現法後法自利利他。云何畢竟及不畢竟自利利他？

blocks.text: The six perfections sorted into merit and wisdom, and why both are needed. A short passage (0485c08) is untranslated.

"Merit is three perfections: giving, precepts, patience. Wisdom is one: the perfection of wisdom. Diligence and concentration belong to both." Diligence in giving, precepts, and the immeasurables is merit; diligence in hearing, reflecting, and cultivating wisdom is wisdom.
"The wish to attain, sustain, and increase them; favourable conditions free of obstruction; prior habituation." Master Cháng Bǎi illustrates the first with the story of a blind monk.

"Resting on merit, bodhisattvas, though cycling through birth and death, are never afflicted by extreme suffering, and can gather beings and benefit them." "Resting on wisdom, the merit gathered is correct." "The ripened body rests on merit; merit rests on wisdom." Hence "merit is the more excellent, wisdom the more unsurpassed". Venerable Miào Jìng explains the distinction.

Bodhisattvas "accumulate wealth through lawful skill and honest effort, and use it with proportion, not defiled by it, not bound by it". They enjoy the fruit of past good actions. And those skilled in the absorptions may "simply rest in the bliss of the present absorption".

quiz.q: "Merit is three perfections." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: the first three of the six
quiz.why: "In brief, merit is three perfections: giving, precepts, and patience." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first three of the six perfections.

quiz.q: "Diligence and concentration belong to both divisions." How do the masters divide concentration?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the immeasurables within concentration are merit, the three samādhis wisdom; Miào Jìng: the immeasurables are cultivated in dhyāna
quiz.why: "Diligence and concentration, one should know, belong to both divisions — partly to merit, and partly to wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: within concentration, the four immeasurables belong to merit, the three samādhis to wisdom. Venerable Miào Jìng: the four immeasurables are cultivated within dhyāna.

quiz.q: The third cause: "prior habituation." How does Venerable Miào Jìng contrast it with the others?
options: the earlier ones are creating now; the third was created in the past
quiz.why: "Third, prior habituation with them." Venerable Miào Jìng: the earlier ones are present — you're creating now; the third is what was created in the past.

quiz.q: The first cause: "the wish to increase" merit. In Master Cháng Bǎi's story of the blind monk threading a needle, what did the Buddha say?
options: I'm never satisfied in cultivating merit
quiz.why: "First, the wish to attain, sustain, and increase them." Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a blind monk calling, "Who wants merit? Thread my needle" — the Buddha came and said: I'm never satisfied in cultivating merit.

quiz.q: "Merit is most excellent, wisdom unsurpassed." The note says neither is secretly ranked higher. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: merit is powerful, but not equal to wisdom
quiz.why: "Merit is the more excellent of the two, and wisdom the more unsurpassed." Venerable Miào Jìng: merit is very powerful, but still not equal to wisdom. The note's "no ranking" differs.

quiz.q: "Skilled in turning (善迴轉) the dhyānas" — rendered "freely entering and leaving." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: turning back deluded thought so it stops — that's calm (skilfully switching calm and insight)
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas already skilled in freely entering and leaving the dhyānas may, wishing simply to obtain the bliss of dwelling in the present dhyāna itself, rest in that dhyāna." Venerable Miào Jìng: turning deluded thought back so it doesn't move — that's calm. The English "entering and leaving" misses the skilful turning between calm and insight.

quiz.q: "The Tathāgatas' present-life nirvāṇa" — rendered "the Tathāgatas' own nirvāṇa." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the present-life nirvāṇa with remainder taught by the Tathāgatas, requiring mundane and supramundane causes; Miào Jìng: the path to nirvāṇa is its cause
quiz.why: "Also, the Tathāgatas' own nirvāṇa realised in this very life rests on every mundane and supramundane conditioned factor." Master Cháng Bǎi: the present-life nirvāṇa with remainder taught by the Tathāgatas requires first cultivating mundane and supramundane causes. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the path of nirvāṇa" is the cause of nirvāṇa. The English reading doesn't match.
